title: FIFA issues statement alleging 'concerted effort' to undermine Infantino after severance claim
dek: FIFA released a statement on August 8, 2026, defending president Gianni Infantino against allegations reported by the Daily Telegraph. The statement characterizes criticism as a coordinated campaign rather than substantive governance concerns. Infantino faces mounting pressure from European football bodies over both personal allegations and a controversial commercial restructuring proposal.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: FIFA issued a statement on August 8, 2026, alleging a 'concerted and ongoing effort' by some parties to undermine the organization and Infantino, following a Daily Telegraph report of alleged personal misconduct.
bottom_line: FIFA's response reframes a governance dispute over commercial rights and institutional authority as a media-driven campaign against Infantino personally. The next critical moment is UEFA's formal reply to FIFA's August 8 statement and whether it signals escalation toward the threatened boycott. Any movement toward a formal vote among FIFA member associations, either supporting or opposing Infantino, would test whether FIFA's claim of democratic mandate holds across all confederations.
body: FIFA released a statement on Saturday, August 8, 2026, alleging a 'concerted and ongoing effort' to 'undermine' the organization and president Gianni Infantino, according to BBC Sport. The statement followed a Daily Telegraph report claiming that Infantino's alleged lover was given a severance payment by UEFA after he allegedly had an affair while serving as the organization's general secretary.

A FIFA spokesperson told the Telegraph that Infantino 'strongly denies' the allegations and that they are 'categorically untrue.' In its official statement, FIFA said: 'Speculation and insinuation should not be presented as fact.' The organization added: 'The Fifa president was democratically elected by Fifa's Member Associations and continues to serve with their mandate.'

FIFA's statement took aim at criticism from European football bodies, stating: 'Those who do not have the support of Fifa's member associations should not seek to achieve through allegation, insinuation or misinformation what they cannot achieve through Fifa's established democratic processes.' The language suggests FIFA views the recent pressure campaign as an attempt to circumvent internal governance structures rather than a legitimate policy dispute.

Infantino has faced increasing pressure from UEFA and European football associations over his aborted Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, which would have created a new company to manage commercial and ticketing rights, with 21 percent sold off to a private investment company. According to BBC reporting, UEFA has said it has lost confidence in Infantino and maintains a threat to boycott FIFA events. UEFA has stated that assurances the FFE plan could not be revived have not been received. The Norwegian Football Federation president, Lise Klaveness, called on Infantino to resign on Friday, August 7, 2026.

Opposition to Infantino is largely concentrated within Europe. However, Infantino retains significant backing elsewhere. The Mexican Football Federation broke ranks with its regional governing body Concacaf to publicly support Infantino, according to BBC reporting. Conmebol, South America's governing body, said it would reject any attempt to remove Infantino without a vote involving all 211 FIFA member countries. Infantino is unanimously backed by the 54 nations of the Confederation of African Football (CAF).

FIFA's statement frames current criticism as a coordinated misinformation campaign rather than engaging substantive challenges to its governance structure or the FFE proposal's terms. UEFA's stated concerns center on both the commercial restructuring and assurances about its future, not solely on the personal allegations. The distinction between institutional criticism and coordinated attack remains disputed between FIFA and its regional critics.
